chunks: And in a copy of al-Safwani — Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Wasiti that he heard Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid, the freed slave of Abu Ja'far, narrating that he (the Imam) made him a witness upon this copied testament:

Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid, the freed slave of Abu Ja'far, testifies that Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) made him a witness that he bequeathed to Ali his son, himself and his sisters, and he made the matter of Musa, when he reaches adulthood, to him. And he made Abdullah ibn al-Musawir a custodian over his estate — the properties, and wealth, and expenditures, and slaves, and other things — until Ali ibn Muhammad reaches adulthood. Abdullah ibn al-Musawir, from that day, came under him (Ali): standing with the matter of his own self and his sisters, and the matter of Musa came to him, standing for himself after the two of them, upon the stipulation of their father regarding his charities which he dispensed. And that was on a Sunday, the third night having passed of Dhu al-Hijja, in the year two hundred and twenty.

Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid wrote his testimony in his own handwriting. And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) — who is al-Juwwani — testified to the same as the testimony of Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid at the beginning of this letter and wrote his testimony by his own hand. Nasr the servant testified and wrote his testimony by his own hand.

key_terms.الرَّقِيقُ: Slaves, bondsmen — part of the estate mentioned in the testament
key_terms.الشَّهَادَةُ: Testimony, witnessing — the formal legal act of bearing witness
key_terms.الصَّدَقَاتُ: Charitable endowments, charitable gifts — the Imam's pious donations with conditions
key_terms.الضِّيَاعُ: Properties, agricultural lands — a form of inherited wealth
key_terms.النُّسْخَةُ: Copy, manuscript — referring to a transmission through al-Safwani's copy
key_terms.الْمَنْسُوخَةُ: Transcribed, copied — describing this testament as a written copy
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: Bequest, testament — the formal legal document designating succession

ai.seo_question: What was the testament of Imam Muhammad al-Jawad designating the 10th Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith records the official testament (wasiyya) of Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (AS), the 9th Imam, designating his son Ali (the future 10th Imam, Ali al-Hadi) as his successor and guardian over his sisters and estate. The document, dated Sunday 3 Dhu al-Hijja 220 AH, was formally witnessed by Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid (the Imam's freed slave), al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Juwwani (a descendant of Imam Ali's family), and Nasr the servant — each writing their testimony in their own hand. This testament is one of the key proofs cited in al-Kafi's chapter on the designation (nass) of the 10th Imam.

en.hubeali: And in a copy of Al Safwany – Muhammad Bin Ja’far Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Al Wasity that he heard Ahmad Bin Abu Khalid a slave of Abu Ja’far, ‘He witnessed upon this copied bequest – ‘

Ahmad Bin Abu Khalid, a slave of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> testifies, ‘I hereby testify that he<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed to Ali<sup>asws</sup> his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> with himself<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> sisters, and made the matter of Musa, when he reaches adulthood, to him<sup>asws</sup>.
And he<sup>asws</sup> made Abdullah Bin Al-Musawir to him on that day to be custodian upon his<sup>asws</sup> legacy from the properties, and wealth, and the expenditure monies, and the slaves, and other than that, until Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) reaches adulthood. Abdullah Bin Al-Musawir, on that day, came to be standing with the matter of his<sup>asws</sup> own self, and his<sup>asws</sup> sisters, and the matter of Musa came to be with him, standing for himself after the two of them, upon the stipulation of their father<sup>asws</sup> regarding his<sup>asws</sup> charities which he<sup>asws</sup> gave with, and that is the day of Sunday the third night of Zil Hijjah, the year two hundred and twenty.

And Ahmad Bin Abu Khalid wrote his testimony by his own handwriting it was witnessed by Al-Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and he is Al-Jawwany, upon the like of the testimony of Ahmad Bin Abu Khalid in the beginning of this letter, and he wrote his testimony by his own hand, Nasr the servant testified and wrote his testimony by his own hand’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far al-Kufi has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Wasiti who has said the following “I heard Ahmad ibn abu Khalid, stating that he (The Imam (a.s.) had appointed him as witness to bear testimony to this documented will in the following words.

“Ahmad ibn abu Khalid, the slave of abu Ja‘far, bears testimony that abu Ja‘far, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) is asked to bear testimony. Testimony to the fact that he has appointed his son, Ali, the executor of his directive wills about himself and bout his sisters. He has placed the affairs of Musa in his charge when he would attain maturity. He has appointed ‘Abdallah ibn al-Musawir as the over seer to his legacy, his estate, property, expenditures and slaves etc., until Ali ibn Muhammad will reach the age of maturity. At such time ‘Abdallah ibn al-Musawir will transfer the overseeing position to him (Ali ibn Muhammad (a.s.)). He thereafter will take charge of his own affairs and sister. The management of the affairs of Musa will also be left to him. Musa will take charge of his own affairs after the two (overseers) according to the conditions set forth by the father of the two of them in the matters his charitable charities. This has been documented on Sunday 3rd dhu al-Hijja, in the year two hundred twenty.

Ahmad ibn abu Khalid has transcribed his own testimony with his own hand writing. He has asked al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah ibn al-Hassan ibn ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.). He is also known as al-Jawani has a testimony just like the testimony of Ahmad ibn abu Khalid at the beginning of this document. He als has written his testimony with his own hand and the witness to bear testimony in the document is Nasr, the servant and he has written his bearing testimony with his own hand.”
